symptoms: Sepsis: life-threatening organ dysfunction due to a dysregulated host response to infection (clinical criteria: increase of >=2 in SOFA score).
Septic shock: sepsis plus, despite adequate fluid resuscitation, persistent hypotension requiring vasopressor to maintain MAP > 65 and lactate > 2.
signs: Young patients may compensate BP until late and have isolated raised lactate; elderly may have isolated hypotension with non-specific lactate levels.
High-risk subgroups: immunocompromised, diabetes mellitus, elderly, pregnant, paediatric.

management_steps.details: Large-bore IV access with balanced crystalloid bolus. Consider early inotrope (adrenaline) to keep MAP > 65. Consider early intubation if needed (correct hypotension and acidosis first). Don't ever forget the glucose.

Features of hypovolaemia / profuse vomiting or diarrhoea: generous fluid bolus 20-30ml/kg. No features of hypovolaemia or fluid overload: gentle fluid bolus 10-20ml/kg. Features of fluid overload: be very cautious with fluids. Don't wait for the fluid bolus to finish before considering inotropic support.

Consider the possible source and take appropriate samples before antibiotics if possible. Give broad-spectrum antibiotics ASAP, within 1 hour. Choice depends on suspected source (e.g. Augmentin for soft tissue, add Azithromycin for atypical pneumonia, Ceftriaxone for meningitis, Piperacillin-Tazobactam for nosocomial infection).

Within 3 hours: measure lactate, obtain blood cultures prior to antibiotics, administer broad-spectrum antibiotics, give 30ml/kg crystalloid bolus for hypotension or lactate > 4 (consider patient factors before giving this volume). Within 6 hours: apply vasopressors to maintain MAP > 65mmHg; if persistent hypotension or initial lactate > 4, re-assess volume status and tissue perfusion and document findings; re-measure lactate if initial level was high.

Monitor vitals, ABG/VBG for improving acidosis, lactate clearance, urine output > 0.5ml/kg/hr. Consider steroids (hydrocortisone 100mg TDS). Appropriate referral; ICU consult if requiring continuous inotrope or ventilatory support.

warnings: Have a high index of clinical suspicion — presentation can be subtle, especially in the very young, elderly, or immunocompromised.
Consider the volume of fluid before giving 30ml/kg — this may be too much for some patients (e.g. heart failure, renal failure).
